science_domain_intervention.paper: Better, Faster, Stronger: Programmatic Skill Learning Best Reduces Agent Cost

upstream_mechanism.paper: Inducing Programmatic Skills for Agentic Tasks

findings.claim: A recent ScienceWorld matched adaptation study removes ASI's replay-based skill verification while stating that all other ASI components are left unchanged. Restoring replay verification improves mean task performance, especially early in training, because broken skills that would regress prior-task behavior are filtered before durable reuse.
findings.scope_guard: The paper provides a near single-variable science-domain admission-verification intervention, but Figure 12 does not print exact per-point numeric values in text; do not invent a precise percentage-point effect.

findings.claim: The original ASI method defines verification as re-executing a rewritten skill-using trajectory for the inducing task and admitting called skills only when task correctness, actual new-skill usage, and skill-call validity all pass. Its official implementation stages candidate functions into the action file behind a temporary backup, runs all generated tests, restores the backup on any failure, and only keeps the staged functions after all tests pass.
findings.scope_guard: The exact public code implements the upstream WebArena ASI mechanism; the ScienceWorld evidence comes from the later adaptation paper. The two together support the admission/rollback mechanism, not identity-frozen receiver-side applicability at each later decision.

protocol_implication.name: TRANSACTIONAL_SKILL_ADMISSION_WITH_REPLAY_PROOF
protocol_implication.rule: Treat generated skill code as staged, not durable authority. Bind candidate digest, inducing-task snapshot, replay/test transcript, verifier revision and pass criteria; commit only after all required checks pass, otherwise restore the pre-stage library exactly.
protocol_implication.causal_strength: science-domain near-single-variable intervention for admission verification plus exact public implementation of upstream staging/test/rollback mechanism
